//   'bashEditDiff'                 the command names the file (path, basename or a parent dir as a path), lists it as a write target, or is a whole-tree formatter (prettier --write ., ruff format, black ., eslint --fix dir/)

Matching: share of `addedNormalized` lines (non-empty) found in an edit event's new content (edit.newContent, edit.addedLines, shell hunks '+' lines) for the same file. Also accept matches against the post-edit file reconstructed from originalFile+structuredPatch when provided. Chains = edits of the file grouped by session; the chain with the best share wins, ties go to a chain containing an Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit over shell-only chains, then to the later chain. `edits` lists EVERY overlapping edit across sessions (MATCHED) or every edit of the file (FILE_LEVEL), sorted by ts, `chain: true` on the winning chain's entries, so `lastEdit` is always the ts of a listed edit (it may belong to another session than the chain). shell_edits with source `bashEditDiff-git`/`bashEditDiff-uncorroborated` are not edits here. `since` (ISO, the merge-base commit time passed by the CLI): a FILE_LEVEL hunk whose every candidate edit predates it becomes UNATTRIBUTED with `reason: 'only edits before the branch base'` (edits: [], lastEdit: null); MATCHED hunks are never downgraded. `checkout` = `edit.checkout` of the edit that defines lastEdit, when present. `intent` = nearest preceding `say` event in the same session before the last edit of the winning chain (<= 200 chars after trimming, more text cut with "…").

added: Flow (src/cli.js, `runCli(argv, io)`): repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; PR metadata via `gh pr view N --json ...` (fallback `gh api repos/o/r/pulls/N`); refs: a merged PR is diffed from its merge commit (`sha^1...sha^2`, or `sha^1...sha` for squash/rebase merges), an open PR from `origin/<base>` to the head branch (HEAD when checked out), no PR from `--base`/origin HEAD/main/master to `--head`/HEAD; base for the diff is `base...head` (merge base). Time window = first commit of `mergeBase..head` minus 2 h (`--window-hours`) .. now. Discovery = deep listCandidateSessions + scoreSession >= 10. Edits made in a git worktree of the repo (incl. `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>`) are remapped onto the repo root; before the rewrite `edit.checkout` records the checkout (worktree root or repo root), and Bash tool events get `ev.checkout` from the directory they ran in (`checkoutOf(effectiveRunDir(command, cwd))`), so runs.js can tell a run made in a checkout that did not contain the edit. Bash events count as runs only when they execute inside the repo (entry cwd or a leading `cd`) or name a path inside it. Events of all selected transcripts are merged and stably sorted by ts before extractRuns/attributeHunks; attributeHunks receives `since` = committer time of the merge base (`repo.mergeBaseTs`). `--evidence FILE` and `--from-note` replay a saved document (render/post only). `--diff FILE` parses a unified diff instead of running git.

added: description: Run hunkproof on the current branch's PR and summarize the unrun hunks
allowed-tools: Bash(node *) Bash(npx hunkproof *) Bash(gh pr view *) Bash(git *) Read
Run hunkproof on the current repository and report what it found. Do not post anything to the PR.

1. Pick the PR: use `$ARGUMENTS` when it is a number, otherwise `gh pr view --json number -q .number`. If the branch has no PR, use `--base <default branch>` (`git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` names it) instead of `--pr`.

2. Run `npx hunkproof --pr <n>` from the repository root. If `npx` is unavailable, run `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/hunkproof.js" --pr <n>`. Exit code 2 means no Claude Code session matched the diff; say so.
- the headline sentence as hunkproof printed it;
- every `UNRUN` hunk as `file:line`, with the check you would run for it (the test file next to it, `npm test`, `pytest <path>`, the linter), or the reason none exists;
- every `RUN_FAIL` hunk with the failing command;
- the number of `FILE_LEVEL` hunks (lines not matched to an edit) and of `UNATTRIBUTED` hunks;
- the path of the HTML report.
5. If the human wants the comment on the PR, they run `npx hunkproof --pr <n> --post` themselves or ask you explicitly; never run `--post` or `--yes` on your own.
Use hunkproof's words: "run after last edit", "unrun", "ran, failed", "ran, outcome not parsed". A passing run after an edit is not a statement that the hunk is correct.

added: You are an agent asked to install hunkproof. Pick the first line that applies and run it; nothing else is needed.
- You run inside Claude Code and the human wants the skill and the `/hunkproof:hunkproof` command:
`claude plugin marketplace add JulienAu/hunkproof && claude plugin install hunkproof@hunkproof`
- You only need the CLI once, in a repository with Node 22 or later:
`npx hunkproof --pr <n>` (no install step; nothing to add to the project).
Both resolve to the same CLI: `bin/hunkproof.js`, zero runtime dependencies, Node 22 ESM. After the plugin install, `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/hunkproof.js"` runs it without npm.

- Run it from the repository root: `npx hunkproof --pr <n>` for a branch with a PR, `npx hunkproof --base main` otherwise. Outputs go to `<repo>/.hunkproof/` (`evidence.json`, `hunkproof.html`, `hunkproof.md`). If it prints `hint: add .hunkproof/ to .gitignore`, pass that hint on; hunkproof does not edit the repository.
- Read the terminal table: one row per hunk with its status (`RUN_PASS`, `RUN_FAIL`, `RUN_UNPARSED`, `UNRUN`, `UNATTRIBUTED`) and the last run after its last edit.
- Never run `--post` without asking the human first; never pass `--yes` for them. The PR comment is public.
- `git` and, for `--pr`, `gh` logged in to the repository's host.
- Claude Code transcripts under `~/.claude/projects` (they are written automatically by Claude Code; hunkproof only reads them).
- No LLM call, no telemetry, no upload of transcripts. The only network calls are `gh` for PR metadata and, after the human confirms, the redacted comment.
- It does not judge whether code is correct. It reports which shell commands ran after each hunk's last edit and what they printed.
`claude plugin uninstall hunkproof@hunkproof && claude plugin marketplace remove hunkproof`

added: description: Stamps every hunk of a pull request with what the agent ran after writing it and lists the hunks that were never run. Use before opening or reviewing a PR written with Claude Code, when someone asks "what did you actually run", "which changes are unrun", "give me a receipt for this PR", or wants a run report posted on a PR. Reads the Claude Code transcripts already on disk; no LLM call, nothing leaves the machine except, on explicit request, a redacted PR comment.
allowed-tools: Bash(node *) Bash(npx hunkproof *) Bash(gh pr view *) Bash(git *) Read

`git diff` shows what changed. hunkproof adds, for every hunk of the diff, the shell command the agent ran after writing it (test runner, linter, type checker, build or script) and its outcome, and marks the hunks with no run at all after their last edit.
From the repository you want to report on:
- The branch has a PR: `npx hunkproof --pr <n> --open` (`--open` opens the HTML report; drop it when no browser is available).
- No PR yet: `npx hunkproof --base main` (or whatever the base branch is).
- Installed as a plugin, with no npm: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/hunkproof.js" --pr <n>` runs the same CLI; it has no dependencies.
- Find the PR number of the current branch with `gh pr view --json number -q .number`.

Outputs land in `<repo>/.hunkproof/`: `evidence.json` (the data), `hunkproof.html` (the report), `hunkproof.md` (the PR comment, not posted). The terminal prints the headline and a table with one row per hunk. If hunkproof prints `hint: add .hunkproof/ to .gitignore`, tell the human; hunkproof never edits the repository itself.
Exit code 2 means no Claude Code session matched the diff; the report is written with every hunk UNATTRIBUTED. Exit code 1 is an error (not a git repository, `gh` not logged in, unknown PR).
| `RUN_PASS` | the last parsed run after the hunk's last edit passed |
| `RUN_UNPARSED` | runs happened after the last edit but none had a readable outcome (moved to background, output piped away) |
| `UNRUN` | no run at all after the last edit |
| `UNATTRIBUTED` | no session edit of this file was found, so nothing is known about runs |

Attribution qualifies the row: `MATCHED` (line-matched: the added lines appear in an edit the agent made), `FILE_LEVEL` (the file was edited in a session but these exact lines were not found in any edit; the run timing is the file's, not the lines'). A run is `targeted` when its command names the file, its stem or its directory, or is a whole-project run with no path argument. The headline counts MATCHED hunks only.

A run "passing" means the command exited 0 with a parsable pass summary. It says nothing about whether the hunk is correct or exercised by that run. Use the tool's words: "run after last edit", "unrun", "ran, failed", "ran, outcome not parsed".
## What to do with UNRUN hunks

1. For each `UNRUN` hunk, run the project's own check for that file, inside the repository checkout that holds the edit: the test file next to it, `npm test`, `pytest <path>`, `go test ./...`, the linter or the type checker. Then run hunkproof again: the run has to come after the hunk's last edit, so run checks last, after the final edit of the file.

2. When no runnable check exists for a hunk (documentation, configuration, a migration that needs a database), say so to the human explicitly: list those hunks by `file:line` and why they stay unrun. Do not edit a file to change its status and do not describe a run that did not happen.
3. `RUN_FAIL` hunks: fix the failure or tell the human which run failed and why.
4. `FILE_LEVEL` hunks: mention that the lines were not matched to an edit, so their status is weaker.
5. `UNATTRIBUTED` hunks were not written in a Claude Code session on this machine, or were written before the branch base; say so instead of guessing who wrote them.

Never run `--post` without asking the human first, and never pass `--yes` on their behalf. The sequence is: run hunkproof, show the human `.hunkproof/hunkproof.md`, ask whether to post, and only then run `npx hunkproof --pr <n> --post`, which previews the comment and asks `Post this comment to PR #N? [y/N]` for the human to answer. The comment is public: it quotes the agent's commands verbatim (after redaction) and, with `--quotes`, the agent's own words.
- Transcripts are read from `~/.claude/projects` on this machine and never uploaded. hunkproof makes no LLM call and no network call except `gh` for PR metadata and, after confirmation, the comment.

- Everything written to the PR goes through redaction (API keys, tokens, private keys, emails, IP addresses, home paths). The HTML and JSON outputs stay local and are more detailed; do not paste `evidence.json` or `hunkproof.html` into a PR or an issue.
- `--quotes` is off by default; leave it off unless the human asks for intent quotes in the comment.

// Pure, zero deps. Consumes Hunk[] (src/diff.js) and Event[] (src/transcript.js).
* Rebuild the post-edit file from originalFile + structuredPatch (diff-style hunks).
* Returns the new file's lines, or null when the inputs are unusable.
if (start < cursor) return null; // overlapping hunks: give up, caller falls back to '+' lines
for (; cursor < start && cursor < orig.length; cursor++) out.push(orig[cursor]);
* Normalized, non-empty set of "new content" lines an edit event contributed to its file.

added: // Usage aggregation and list-price cost estimate for `usage` events.
// Transcript facts this module relies on (checked against real lines):
// - every content block of one API response is written as its own
//   `assistant` line carrying the same message.id + requestId, with the usage
//   object repeated (output_tokens grows block after block), so one API call
//   appears up to several times and the LAST/largest values are the real ones;
// - `<synthetic>` assistant lines have no requestId: fall back to uuid;
// - model ids can carry a date suffix (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001).
// Attached to every dollar figure. It says what the number is (a list-price
// computation) without asserting the reader's billing plan.
export const COST_LABEL = 'what these tokens would cost at Anthropic API list prices; not a bill (subscription plans have no per-token charge)';
* Resolve the price row for a model id: exact key first, then the longest
* key that is a '-' delimited prefix of the id. Returns null when unknown.
if (model.startsWith(key + '-') && (best === null || key.length > best.length)) best = key;
/** USD list price of one usage bucket, or null when the model is unpriced. */
return null; // no identity at all: counted as its own call
* Dedupes by `${messageId}|${requestId}` (fallback uuid) keeping, per key, the
* maximum of each token field (the repeated lines are cumulative snapshots).
call = { model, input: 0, output: 0, cacheWrite: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite1h: 0 };
for (const f of FIELDS) call[f] = Math.max(call[f], num(ev.usage[f]));
const totals = { input: 0, output: 0, cacheWrite: 0, cacheRead: 0, messages: 0 };
const row = (byModel[call.model] ??= { input: 0, output: 0, cacheWrite: 0, cacheRead: 0, messages: 0 });

// Pure parser (parseUnifiedDiff) + a thin git wrapper (gitDiffHunks). Zero deps.
/** trim + collapse internal whitespace runs to one space */

* `a/P b/P`; we look for a split point where both halves agree. Otherwise we fall back to the last ` b/`.
* Parse a unified diff (as produced by `git diff`, any -U value) into Hunk[].
* Binary files are skipped and counted in opts.stats.binary / opts.stats.binaryFiles.
* Renames keep the NEW path as `file`/`relFile` and expose `oldFile`/`oldRelFile`.
if (!repoRoot) throw new Error('parseUnifiedDiff: repoRoot is required');
let file = null; // current file state
let hunk = null; // current hunk being filled
const pushHunk = () => { if (hunk) { hunks.push(hunk); hunk = null; } };
file = { oldRel, newRel, kind: 'modify', binary: false, sawHeaders: false };
if (!file) continue; // preamble or non-git diff text before first header
if (raw.startsWith('\\')) { continue; } // "\ No newline at end of file"
pushHunk(); // counts consumed (or a new header): hand the line to the file-level parser
else if (raw.startsWith(' ')) { hunk.context.push(raw.slice(1)); hunk.remainOld -= 1; hunk.remainNew -= 1; continue; }
else if (raw === '') { hunk.context.push(''); hunk.remainOld -= 1; hunk.remainNew -= 1; continue; } // bare empty context line (some tools strip the space)
else { pushHunk(); /* unknown line: let the file-level parser look at it */ }
if (raw.startsWith('Binary files ') || raw.startsWith('GIT binary patch')) { file.binary = true; continue; }
if (raw.startsWith('new file mode')) { file.kind = 'add'; st.newFiles += 1; continue; }
if (raw.startsWith('deleted file mode')) { file.kind = 'delete'; st.deletedFiles += 1; continue; }
if (raw.startsWith('rename from ')) { file.oldRel = unquoteGitPath(raw.slice('rename from '.length)); file.kind = 'rename'; st.renames += 1; continue; }
if (raw.startsWith('rename to ')) { file.newRel = unquoteGitPath(raw.slice('rename to '.length)); file.kind = 'rename'; continue; }
if (raw.startsWith('copy from ') || raw.startsWith('copy to ')) { if (raw.startsWith('copy to ')) file.newRel = unquoteGitPath(raw.slice('copy to '.length)); continue; }

import { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
// Plain-English footers. They follow the vocabulary rule in CLAUDE.md (say
// "run after last edit", "unrun", "ran, failed", "ran, outcome not parsed").
hunk: 'A hunk is one contiguous block of added or removed lines in the diff between the base and head commits (git diff -U0). Its id is the file and the first new line number.',

attribution: 'MATCHED (line-matched): most of the added lines appear in an edit the agent made to this file during a session; only these hunks count as attributed in the headline. FILE_LEVEL: the agent edited this file in a session, but the added lines could not be found in any edit, so the run timing is relative to the file\'s last edit, not to the lines. UNATTRIBUTED: no session edit of this file was found, or the only edits of the file predate the branch base commit. Working-tree changes a shell command cannot have written (a merge, files changed by another agent while the command ran) are not counted as edits.',

run: 'A run is a shell command that executes code: a test runner, a linter, a type checker, a build, or a direct script invocation. Commands that only write files are not runs, nor are hunkproof\'s own invocations. Outcome is pass, fail, or unparsed when the exit status and output could not be read (including commands moved to the background).',

status: 'Decided by the last run after the hunk\'s last edit whose outcome was parsed, targeted runs first; a run made in another checkout than the edit (a git worktree) never decides. RUN_PASS: that run passed. RUN_FAIL: it failed ("ran, failed"). RUN_UNPARSED: runs happened after the last edit but none had a parsable outcome ("ran, outcome not parsed"). UNRUN: no run at all after the last edit. UNATTRIBUTED: the hunk could not be tied to a session edit, so nothing is known about runs.',

targeted: 'A run is targeted when the command names the file, its stem or its parent directory, or when it is a whole-project run with no path arguments. The strict count only accepts targeted runs after the last edit.',

cost: `Token counts come from the session transcripts, deduplicated per API call. The dollar figure is ${COST_LABEL}; it comes from a dated public price table and is not what was billed. // Pure string -> string. Placeholders never match the patterns themselves, so
// '/' is left out on purpose so file paths never merge into one long run; a
// standard base64 secret containing '/' is still caught piecewise when a piece
// is 32+ chars, and the prefixed patterns above catch the common key formats.
// Bind-all and loopback addresses identify nobody.
/** True when a long [A-Za-z0-9+/_-] run looks like a credential, not an identifier. */
// Identifiers are mostly letters of one case, with few digits and no +/.
// A dashed or underscored slug like some-long-package-name-v2-release-candidate.
// An identifier made of several short separated chunks (feat_block12_L3x_raw);
// a random url-safe token of this length rarely holds three separators.
* Order: PEM blocks, JWTs, Authorization schemes, prefixed API keys, emails,
* long high-entropy tokens (>=32 hex or base64-ish chars), IPv4, home paths.
for (const re of PREFIXED_RE) out = out.replace(re, '[REDACTED:key]');

// The comment is public, so it stays small and quotes as little agent text as

// (default 60,000) by dropping commands, then the per-hunk list.
// pick a fence longer than any backtick run inside
out.push(`**Unrun hunks** · edited by the agent, no run after the last edit`);
out.push('| Hunk | Lines | Last edit (UTC) | Rewrites | Attribution |');

out.push(`**Unattributed hunks** · ${unattributed.length}, no agent edit matched: ${list.map((h) => hunkLink(h, blobBase)).join(', ')}${more ? `, … ${more} more` : ''}`);
const deciding = new Map(); // key -> run
out.push(`<summary>All ${hunks.length} hunks with the run that decided their status</summary>`);
if (h.status === 'UNATTRIBUTED') head += h.reason ? ` · no agent edit matched (${h.reason})` : ' · no agent edit matched';
else if (!runs.length) head += ` · last edit ${fmtTime(h.lastEdit)} UTC`;
out.push(`<summary>Deciding runs · ${deciding.size} distinct${total !== null ? ` of ${total} ${total === 1 ? 'run' : 'runs'} recorded` : ''}</summary>`);
out.push(`_${hunks.length} hunks not listed here: the comment would exceed GitHub's size limit. Open hunkproof.html locally or run ${mdCode(reproCommand(ev))}._`);

out.push(`<sub>hunkproof ${(ev.tool && ev.tool.version) || ''} · generated ${fmtDateTime(ev.generatedAt)} · transcripts stay on the machine; this comment was redacted before posting; agent commands are quoted verbatim.</sub>`);

usage.label: what these tokens would cost at Anthropic API list prices; not a bill (subscription plans have no per-token charge)

definitions.hunk: A hunk is one contiguous block of added or removed lines in the diff between the base and head commits (git diff -U0). Its id is the file and the first new line number.
definitions.attribution: MATCHED (line-matched): most of the added lines appear in an edit the agent made to this file during a session; only these hunks count as attributed in the headline. FILE_LEVEL: the agent edited this file in a session, but the added lines could not be found in any edit, so the run timing is relative to the file's last edit, not to the lines. UNATTRIBUTED: no session edit of this file was found, or the only edits of the file predate the branch base commit. Working-tree changes a shell command cannot have written (a merge, files changed by another agent while the command ran) are not counted as edits.
definitions.run: A run is a shell command that executes code: a test runner, a linter, a type checker, a build, or a direct script invocation. Commands that only write files are not runs, nor are hunkproof's own invocations. Outcome is pass, fail, or unparsed when the exit status and output could not be read (including commands moved to the background).
definitions.status: Decided by the last run after the hunk's last edit whose outcome was parsed, targeted runs first; a run made in another checkout than the edit (a git worktree) never decides. RUN_PASS: that run passed. RUN_FAIL: it failed ("ran, failed"). RUN_UNPARSED: runs happened after the last edit but none had a parsable outcome ("ran, outcome not parsed"). UNRUN: no run at all after the last edit. UNATTRIBUTED: the hunk could not be tied to a session edit, so nothing is known about runs.
definitions.targeted: A run is targeted when the command names the file, its stem or its parent directory, or when it is a whole-project run with no path arguments. The strict count only accepts targeted runs after the last edit.
definitions.cost: Token counts come from the session transcripts, deduplicated per API call. The dollar figure is what these tokens would cost at Anthropic API list prices; not a bill (subscription plans have no per-token charge); it comes from a dated public price table and is not what was billed.
